headline: Robustness of sequence models and evolutionary search on genomic data
label: Machine Learning For Genomic Sequences
summary: Sequence models for regulatory and methylation data are now tested under distribution shift and paired with interpretable, evidence-gated processing.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the application of machine learning and search methods to genomic sequence data, with attention to robustness, diversity, and interpretability of decisions. One item benchmarks CNN, BiLSTM and transformer architectures for DNA regulatory sequence prediction under simulated and MPRA-based biological and technical distribution shifts, directly testing how learned sequence models hold up outside their training conditions. A second frames motif discovery as a quality-diversity problem, using MAP-Elites to evolve PWM motifs on human liver CTCF ChIP-seq data and recover diverse high-fitness variants. A third, Y-Trim, addresses preprocessing in single-stranded bisulfite sequencing by separating trim admission from cut placement for Adaptase tails. Across these items, the new elements are explicit evaluation under shift, maintenance of candidate diversity, and gated, interpretable processing steps. The items do not establish generalization beyond the reported datasets.
